reading.intro: 本篇主题：塑料藏品的保存难题。先读题干，圈出关键词；回原文找证据句，再用主体、范围、方向排除。

paragraphs.en: People often complain that plastics are too durable. Water bottles, shopping bags, and other trash litter the planet, from Mount Everest to the Mariana Trench, because plastics are everywhere and don't break down easily. But some plastic materials change over time. They crack and frizzle. They "weep" out additives. They melt into sludge. All of which creates huge headaches for institutions, such as museums, trying to preserve culturally important objects. The variety of plastic objects at risk is dizzying: early radios, avant-garde sculptures, celluloid animation stills from Disney films, the first artificial heart.
paragraphs.zh: 人们常常抱怨塑料太耐用了。 从珠穆朗玛峰到马里亚纳海沟，水瓶、购物袋及其他垃圾遍布地球，因为塑料无处不在，而且不易分解。 然而，有些塑料材料会随着时间推移而发生变化。 它们会开裂、卷曲。 它们会“渗出”添加剂。 它们还会融化成黏稠的浆状物。 所有这些变化都给博物馆等试图保存具有文化价值物品的机构带来了巨大的难题。 面临损坏风险的塑料制品种类多得令人眼花缭乱：早期收音机、先锋派雕塑、迪士尼电影的赛璐珞动画静帧，乃至第一颗人造心脏。

paragraphs.en: Certain artifacts are especially vulnerable because some pioneers in plastic art didn't always know how to mix ingredients properly, says Thea van Oosten, a polymer chemist who, until retiring a few years ago, worked for decades at the Cultural Heritage Agency of the Netherlands (RCE). "It's like baking a cake: If you don't have exact amounts, it goes wrong," she says. "The object you make is already a time bomb."
paragraphs.zh: 聚合物化学家西娅·范·奥斯滕说，某些艺术品格外脆弱，是因为一些塑料艺术的先驱当年并不总是知道怎样正确调配原料；她在几年前退休之前，曾在荷兰文化遗产局（RCE）工作数十年。 她说：“这就像烤蛋糕一样：各成分的用量不精确，就会出问题。” “这样制成的物品从一开始就是一颗定时炸弹。”

paragraphs.en: And sometimes, it's not the artist's fault. In the 1960s, the Italian artist Piero Gilardi began to create hundreds of bright, colorful foam pieces. Those pieces included small beds of roses and other items as well as a few dozen "nature carpets"—large rectangles decorated with foam pumpkins, cabbages, and watermelons. He wanted viewers to walk around on the carpets—which meant they had to be durable.
paragraphs.zh: 而且有时候，问题并不在艺术家。 20 世纪 60 年代，意大利艺术家皮耶罗·吉拉尔迪开始创作数百件色彩鲜艳的泡沫塑料作品。 这些作品包括小片玫瑰花圃等物件，也包括几十张“自然地毯”——装饰着泡沫塑料南瓜、卷心菜和西瓜的大幅长方形作品。 他希望参观者能在这些地毯上走动——这意味着它们必须经久耐用。

paragraphs.en: Unfortunately, the polyurethane foam he used is inherently unstable. It's especially vulnerable to light damage, and by the mid-1990s, Gilardi's pumpkins, roses, and other figures were splitting and crumbling. Museums locked some of them away in the dark.
paragraphs.zh: 遗憾的是，他使用的聚氨酯泡沫本身就不稳定。 这种材料尤其容易受到光照损害；到 20 世纪 90 年代中期，吉拉尔迪作品中的南瓜、玫瑰和其他造型都已开始开裂、碎裂。 博物馆把其中一些作品锁进了不见光的地方。

paragraphs.en: So van Oosten and colleagues worked to preserve Gilardi's sculptures. They infused some with stabilizing and consolidating chemicals. Van Oosten calls those chemicals "sunscreens" because their goal was to prevent further light damage and rebuild worn polymer fibers. She is proud that several sculptures have even gone on display again, albeit sometimes beneath protective cases.
paragraphs.zh: 于是，范·奥斯滕及其同事着手保护吉拉尔迪的雕塑。 他们给部分作品注入稳定剂和加固剂。 范·奥斯滕把这些化学制剂称为“防晒霜”，因为它们旨在防止光照造成进一步损害，并修复已经磨损的聚合物纤维。 令她自豪的是，有几件雕塑甚至已经重新展出，尽管有时需要放在保护罩下。

paragraphs.en: Despite success stories like van Oosten's, preservation of plastics will likely get harder. Old objects continue to deteriorate. Worse, biodegradable plastics, designed to disintegrate, are increasingly common.
paragraphs.zh: 尽管有范·奥斯滕这样的成功案例，塑料制品的保存工作很可能仍会变得更加艰难。 旧物件仍在不断劣化。 更糟的是，本来就被设计成会分解的可生物降解塑料正变得越来越常见。

paragraphs.en: And more is at stake here than individual objects. Joana Lia Ferreira, an assistant professor of conservation and restoration at the NOVA School of Science and Technology, notes that archaeologists first defined the great material ages of human history—Stone Age, Iron Age, and so on—after examining artifacts in museums. We now live in an age of plastic, she says, "and what we decide to collect today, what we decide to preserve...will have a strong impact on how in the future we'll be seen."
paragraphs.zh: 而这里关系到的，远不止一件件具体物品的存亡。 诺瓦科技学院文物保护与修复专业助理教授若阿娜·莉娅·费雷拉指出，考古学家正是在研究了博物馆藏品之后，才首次划分出人类历史上以材料命名的各大时代，例如石器时代、铁器时代等。 她说，我们如今生活在一个塑料时代，“而我们今天决定收藏什么、保存什么……将深刻影响未来的人如何看待我们”。

questions.stem: According to Paragraph 1, museums are faced with difficulties in
questions.explain:
正确项：maintaining their plastic items. 原文中的 preserve culturally important objects 表明博物馆正设法保存具有文化价值的物品；前文列举塑料开裂、渗出添加剂和融成浆状物等问题，说明难点在于维护、保存塑料藏品。maintaining 是对 preserve 的同义改写。
其他选项：B. obtaining durable plastic artifacts.：原文说塑料藏品已经存在，问题是部分材料会随时间劣化，并未说博物馆难以“获得”耐用藏品，属于行为偷换。；C. handling outdated plastic exhibits.：文中讨论的是藏品材质老化，而不是展品内容“过时”；outdated 偷换了 change over time 的含义。；D. classifying their plastic collections.：原文虽列举藏品种类繁多，却没有说博物馆难以对其分类；把“种类多”擅自推成“分类困难”。
questions.evidence: All of which creates huge headaches for institutions, such as museums, trying to preserve culturally important objects.

questions.explain:
正确项：inherently flawed. 一些早期艺术家未能正确调配原料，使制成的作品从一开始就是一颗“定时炸弹”。因此，这些塑料物品具有制作之初便存在的内在缺陷；inherently flawed 概括了 already a time bomb 及其成因。
其他选项：A. immune to decay.：原文明确说这些艺术品 especially vulnerable，即非常容易劣化；“不会腐坏”与原文相反。；B. improperly shaped.：问题在原料配比不当，不在作品外形塑造不当，属于偷换缺陷类型。；D. complex in structure.：原文没有评价作品结构是否复杂，仅以烤蛋糕比喻原料用量必须准确，属于无中生有。
questions.evidence:
Certain artifacts are especially vulnerable because some pioneers in plastic art didn't always know how to mix ingredients properly, says Thea van Oosten, a polymer chemist who, until retiring a few years ago, worked for decades at the Cultural Heritage Agency of the Netherlands (RCE).

questions.explain:

questions.stem: The author thinks that preservation of plastics is
questions.explain:

其他选项：A. costly.：文中介绍了保存技术和难度，却没有讨论成本高低，属于无中生有。；B. unworthy.：末段强调保存塑料藏品具有记录历史的意义，作者并不认为此事“不值得”，与文意相反。；C. unpopular.：原文没有调查公众或业内对塑料保存工作的欢迎程度，属于无关信息。

questions.explain:

reading.topic: Z 世代是否仍应把大学学历视为默认选择
reading.intro: 本篇主题：Z 世代是否仍应把大学学历视为默认选择。先读题干，圈出关键词；回原文找证据句，再用主体、范围、方向排除。

paragraphs.en: As the latest crop of students pen their undergraduate application form and weigh up their options, it may be worth considering just how the point, purpose and value of a degree has changed and what Generation Z need to consider as they start the third stage of their educational journey.
paragraphs.zh: 当最新一批学生填写本科申请表、权衡各种选择时，或许值得认真思考：大学学位的意义、目的与价值究竟发生了怎样的变化，以及 Z 世代在开启教育历程的第三阶段时需要考虑什么。

paragraphs.en: Millennials were told that if you did well in school, got a decent degree, you would be set up for life. But that promise has been found wanting. As degrees became universal, they became devalued. Education was no longer a secure route of social mobility. Today, 28 per cent of graduates in the UK are in non-graduate roles, a percentage which is double the average among the OECD countries.
paragraphs.zh: 千禧一代曾被告知，只要在学校表现良好、取得一个不错的学位，一辈子的生活就有了保障。 然而事实证明，这一承诺并未兑现预期。 随着大学学位日益普及，其价值也随之降低。 教育不再是一条稳妥实现社会阶层流动的途径。 如今，英国有 28% 的大学毕业生从事并不要求大学学历的工作，这一比例是经济合作与发展组织成员国平均水平的两倍。

paragraphs.en: This is not to say that there is no point in getting a degree, but rather stress that a degree is not for everyone, that the switch from classroom to lecture hall is not an inevitable one and that other options are available.
paragraphs.zh: 这并不是说取得学位毫无意义，而是要强调：学位并不适合每一个人；从中学课堂转入大学讲堂并非必然选择；此外还有其他道路可走。

paragraphs.en: Thankfully, there are signs that this is already happening, with Generation Z seeking to learn from their millennial predecessors, even if parents and teachers tend to be still set in the degree mindset. Employers have long seen the advantages of hiring school leavers who often prove themselves to be more committed and loyal employees than graduates. Many too are seeing the advantages of scrapping a degree requirement for certain roles.
paragraphs.zh: 令人欣慰的是，已经有迹象表明这种转变正在发生：Z 世代正努力从千禧一代前辈的经历中吸取教训，尽管父母和教师往往仍受“唯学位”思维束缚。 长期以来，雇主一直看得到聘用中学毕业后直接就业者的好处；事实常常证明，他们比大学毕业生对工作更投入、对雇主更忠诚。 许多雇主也开始认识到，取消某些岗位的学历要求是有好处的。

paragraphs.en: For those for whom a degree is the desired route, consider that this may well be the first of many. In this age of generalists, it pays to have specific knowledge or skills. Postgraduates now earn 40 per cent more than graduates. When more and more of us have a degree, it makes sense to have two.
paragraphs.zh: 对于那些确实希望走学位教育这条路的人，应当想到：这个学位很可能只是以后多个学位中的第一个。 在这个通才辈出的时代，拥有某一领域的专门知识或技能会很有价值。 如今，拥有研究生学历的人比只有本科文凭的毕业生收入高 40%。 当越来越多的人都有一个学位时，再取得一个学位便是合乎情理的选择。

paragraphs.en: It is unlikely that Generation Z will be done with education at 18 or 21; they will need to be constantly upskilling throughout their career to stay employable. It has been estimated that this generation, due to the pressures of technology, the wish for personal fulfilment and desire for diversity, will work for 17 different employers over the course of their working life and have five different careers. Education, and not just knowledge gained on campus, will be a core part of Generation Z's career trajectory.
paragraphs.zh: Z 世代不太可能在 18 岁或 21 岁时就结束教育；为了始终具备就业竞争力，他们需要在整个职业生涯中不断提升技能。 据估计，由于技术发展带来的压力、实现个人价值的愿望以及追求多样性的需求，这一代人在整个职业生涯中将为 17 个不同的雇主工作，并经历 5 种不同的职业。 教育，而且不只是校园里获得的知识，将成为 Z 世代职业发展轨迹的核心组成部分。

paragraphs.en: Older generations often talk about their degree in the present and personal tense: "I am a geographer" or "I am a classicist." Their sons or daughters would never say such a thing; it's as if they already know that their degree won't define them in the same way.
paragraphs.zh: 老一辈人谈起自己的学位时，常使用一种现在时的、与个人身份紧密相连的说法：“我是一名地理学家”或“我是一名古典学者”。 他们的子女绝不会这样说；仿佛年轻一代已经明白，学位不会再以同样的方式定义自己的身份。

questions.stem: The author suggests that Generation Z should
options: be careful in choosing a college.
be diligent at each educational stage.
reassess the necessity of college education.
questions.explain:
正确项：reassess the necessity of college education. 作者要求 Z 世代重新思考学位的意义与价值，并明确指出大学“不适合每个人”、从中学升入大学“并非必然”、还存在其他选择。因此，他们应重新评估自己是否有必要接受大学教育。
其他选项：A. be careful in choosing a college.：文章讨论的是是否需要走大学这条路，而非在不同大学之间谨慎择校，缩小并偷换了思考范围。；B. be diligent at each educational stage.：作者强调教育路径选择和持续学习，没有要求学生在每一教育阶段都更加勤奋，属于无中生有。；D. postpone their undergraduate application.：开头虽以填写本科申请表为背景，却未建议推迟申请；“重新考虑必要性”不等于“延后申请”。
questions.evidence:
As the latest crop of students pen their undergraduate application form and weigh up their options, it may be worth considering just how the point, purpose and value of a degree has changed and what Generation Z need to consider as they start the third stage of their educational journey.
This is not to say that there is no point in getting a degree, but rather stress that a degree is not for everyone, that the switch from classroom to lecture hall is not an inevitable one and that other options are available.

questions.stem: The percentage of UK graduates in non-graduate roles reflects
options: the shrinking value of a degree.
the desired route of social mobility.
questions.explain:
正确项：the shrinking value of a degree. 作者先作出“学位越普及，价值越低”的判断，随后用英国 28% 的毕业生从事非学历岗位这一数据加以证明。该比例反映的是大学学位在就业市场上的区分度和价值正在下降。
其他选项：A. Millennials' opinion about work.：数据反映的是毕业生就业岗位与学历不匹配的客观状况，不是千禧一代对工作的主观看法，属于性质偷换。；C. public discontent with education.：原文没有提及公众对教育不满，更没有用该比例衡量公众态度，属于无中生有。；D. the desired route of social mobility.：原文说教育 was no longer a secure route of social mobility，强调这条道路不再可靠；选项却把它说成理想途径，与上下文判断相反。
questions.evidence:
As degrees became universal, they became devalued.
Today, 28 per cent of graduates in the UK are in non-graduate roles, a percentage which is double the average among the OECD countries.

questions.stem: The author considers it a good sign that
options: Generation Z are seeking to earn a decent degree.
school leavers are willing to be skilled workers.
employers are taking a realistic attitude to degree.
parents are changing their minds about education.
questions.explain:
正确项：employers are taking a realistic attitude to degree. Thankfully 标明作者的肯定态度；后文说雇主重视中学毕业后直接就业者的实际表现，并开始取消某些岗位的学历要求。这说明雇主不再机械地把学位当作所有岗位的必要条件，而是采取更务实的态度。
其他选项：A. Generation Z are seeking to earn a decent degree.：Z 世代正在做的是从千禧一代的经历中吸取教训、考虑其他道路，不是努力取得一个“不错的学位”，与段落主旨不符。；B. school leavers are willing to be skilled workers.：原文说中学毕业后直接就业者往往表现得更投入、更忠诚，没有说他们愿意成为技术工人，偷换了品质和职业类型。；D. parents are changing their minds about education.：原文说父母和教师仍然固守学位思维，选项称其正在改变观念，与原文相反。
questions.evidence:
Thankfully, there are signs that this is already happening, with Generation Z seeking to learn from their millennial predecessors, even if parents and teachers tend to be still set in the degree mindset.
Many too are seeing the advantages of scrapping a degree requirement for certain roles.

questions.stem: It is advised in Paragraph 5 that those with one degree should
options: make an early decision on their career.
further their studies in a specific field.
questions.explain:
正确项：further their studies in a specific field. 作者认为第一个学位可能只是多个学位中的第一个，并指出在通才时代拥有专门知识或技能更有利。当一个学位已十分普遍时，再读一个学位具有合理性。因此，已有一个学位者应在特定领域继续深造。
其他选项：A. make an early decision on their career.：本段讨论用后续学位获取专门知识，没有要求尽早确定职业；下段反而预测 Z 世代会多次转换职业。；B. attend on-the-job training programs.：文中建议继续取得学位并深化专门知识，未提及在职培训项目，属于无中生有。；C. team up with high-paid postgraduates.：研究生收入更高是支持继续深造的数据，并非建议本科毕业生与高收入研究生合作，误读了比较关系。
questions.evidence:
For those for whom a degree is the desired route, consider that this may well be the first of many.
In this age of generalists, it pays to have specific knowledge or skills.
When more and more of us have a degree, it makes sense to have two.

questions.stem: What can be concluded about Generation Z from the last two paragraphs?
options: Degrees will no longer appeal them.
They will have a limited choice of jobs.
questions.explain:
正确项：Lifelong learning will define them. 作者判断 Z 世代不会在 18 岁或 21 岁结束教育，而要在整个职业生涯中不断提升技能，并明确说教育将是其职业轨迹的核心部分。这正是“终身学习将成为其鲜明特征”的含义。
其他选项：B. They will make qualified educators.：Education 指 Z 世代持续接受教育和学习，不是说他们会从事教育工作或成为合格教师，混淆了学习者与教育者。；C. Degrees will no longer appeal them.：文章并未说学位失去吸引力；第五段甚至建议适合大学道路的人取得更多学位。作者否定的是一个学位定义终身，而不是学位本身。；D. They will have a limited choice of jobs.：文中预测他们一生会服务 17 个雇主、经历 5 种职业，体现职业变化多而非选择受限，与原文不符。
questions.evidence:
It is unlikely that Generation Z will be done with education at 18 or 21; they will need to be constantly upskilling throughout their career to stay employable.
Education, and not just knowledge gained on campus, will be a core part of Generation Z's career trajectory.

reading.title: Text 3
reading.en_title: Enlightening, challenging, stimulating, fun. These were some of the wo…
reading.cn_title: 艺术与科学合作的价值
reading.topic: 艺术与科学合作的价值
reading.intro: 本篇主题：艺术与科学合作的价值。先读题干，圈出关键词；回原文找证据句，再用主体、范围、方向排除。

paragraphs.en: Enlightening, challenging, stimulating, fun. These were some of the words that Nature readers used to describe their experience of art-science collaborations in a series of articles on partnerships between artists and researchers. Nearly 40% of the roughly 350 people who responded to an accompanying poll said they had collaborated with artists; and almost all said they would consider doing so in future.
paragraphs.zh: 富有启发、颇具挑战、激发思考而且妙趣横生。 在一组探讨艺术家与研究人员合作关系的文章中，《自然》杂志的读者用上述词语来形容他们参与艺术与科学合作的体验。 在参加配套调查的大约 350 人中，近 40% 表示自己曾与艺术家合作；而且几乎所有人都表示，将来会考虑开展这类合作。

paragraphs.en: Such an encouraging result is not surprising. Scientists are increasingly seeking out visual artists to help them communicate their work to new audiences. "Artists help scientists reach a broader audience and make emotional connections that enhance learning," one respondent said.
paragraphs.zh: 这样令人鼓舞的调查结果并不出人意料。 科学家越来越主动寻找视觉艺术家，帮助自己向新的受众传播科研成果。 一名调查参与者说：“艺术家帮助科学家触及更广泛的受众，并建立能够促进理解与学习的情感联系。”

paragraphs.en: One example of how artists and scientists have together rocked the scenes came last month when the Sydney Symphony Orchestra performed a reworked version of Antonio Vivaldi's The Four Seasons. They reimagined the 300-year-old score by injecting the latest climate prediction data for each season—provided by Monash University's Climate Change Communication Research Hub. The performance was a creative call to action ahead of November's United Nations Climate Change Conference in Glasgow, UK.
paragraphs.zh: 艺术家与科学家携手带来轰动效果的一个例子出现在上个月：悉尼交响乐团演奏了安东尼奥·维瓦尔第《四季》的改编版。 他们把莫纳什大学气候变化传播研究中心提供的各季最新气候预测数据融入这部有 300 年历史的乐谱，从而对其作出全新诠释。 在 11 月联合国气候变化大会于英国格拉斯哥召开之前，这场演出以富有创意的方式发出了行动号召。

paragraphs.en: But a genuine partnership must be a two-way street. Fewer artists than scientists responded to the Nature poll, however, several respondents noted that artists do not simply assist scientists with their communication requirements. Nor should their work be considered only as an object of study. The alliances are most valuable when scientists and artists have a shared stake in a project, are able to jointly design it and can critique each other's work. Such an approach can both prompt new research as well as result in powerful art.
paragraphs.zh: 但真正的合作关系必须是双向的。 不过，参与《自然》杂志调查的艺术家少于科学家；几名调查参与者指出，艺术家并不只是帮助科学家满足科研传播需求的助手。 艺术家的作品也不应仅仅被视为研究对象。 当科学家和艺术家共同关心项目的成败，能够一起设计项目并相互评议对方的工作时，这种合作关系才最有价值。 这种合作方式既能推动新的研究，也能催生具有感染力的艺术作品。

paragraphs.en: More than half a century ago, the Massachusetts Institute of Technology opened its Center for Advanced Visual Studies (CAVS) to explore the role of technology in culture. The founders deliberately focused their projects around light—hence the "visual studies" in the name. Light was a something that both artists and scientists had an interest in, and therefore could form the basis of collaboration. As science and technology progressed, and divided into more sub-disciplines, the centre was simultaneously looking to a time when leading researchers could also be artists, writers and poets, and vice versa.
paragraphs.zh: 半个多世纪前，麻省理工学院成立了高级视觉研究中心（CAVS），以探索技术在文化中的作用。 创办者有意让各个项目围绕“光”展开，因此中心名称中才有“视觉研究”一词。 光是艺术家与科学家都感兴趣的事物，因此能够成为双方合作的基础。 随着科学技术不断发展并细分出更多学科，这一中心同时也在展望一个时代：顶尖研究人员也可以成为艺术家、作家和诗人，反之亦然。

paragraphs.en: Nature's poll findings suggest that this trend is as strong as ever, but, to make a collaboration work, both sides need to invest time, and embrace surprise and challenge. The reach of art-science tie-ups needs to go beyond the necessary purpose of research communication, and participants must not fall into the trap of stereotyping each other. Artists and scientists alike are immersed in discovery and invention, and challenge and critique are core to both, too.
paragraphs.zh: 《自然》杂志的调查结果表明，这一合作趋势依旧十分强劲；但是，要让合作真正奏效，双方都需要投入时间，并欣然接受意外与挑战。 艺术与科学合作的作用范围需要超越科研传播这一必要目的，参与者也绝不能落入彼此刻板化的陷阱。 艺术家和科学家同样投身于发现与创造，挑战和批判性评议对双方而言也都至关重要。

questions.stem: According to Paragraph 1, art-science collaborations have
questions.explain:
正确项：received favorable responses. 读者用 enlightening、stimulating、fun 等褒义词描述合作体验，几乎所有调查参与者又都愿意考虑未来合作。这些评价与意愿共同表明艺术科学合作获得了积极反响。
其他选项：A. caught the attention of critics.：参与调查的是《自然》读者和有合作经历的人，文中没有提到评论家关注这些合作，属于主体偷换。；C. promoted academic publishing.：系列文章只是调查的发布背景，原文没有说合作促进了学术出版，属于因场景词而产生的无端推断。；D. sparked heated public disputes.：首段呈现的是积极评价和未来合作意愿，没有“激烈公众争论”，与语气相反。
questions.evidence:
Enlightening, challenging, stimulating, fun.
These were some of the words that Nature readers used to describe their experience of art-science collaborations in a series of articles on partnerships between artists and researchers.
Nearly 40% of the roughly 350 people who responded to an accompanying poll said they had collaborated with artists; and almost all said they would consider doing so in future.

questions.stem: The reworked version of The Four Seasons is mentioned to show that
options: art can offer audiences easy access to science.
science can help with the expression of emotions.
public participation in science has a promising future.
art is effective in facilitating scientific innovations.
questions.explain:
正确项：art can offer audiences easy access to science. 演出把各季最新气候预测数据融入公众熟悉的音乐作品，并以艺术形式发出应对气候变化的行动号召。该例说明艺术能把科学信息转化为受众更容易接触和感受的内容。
其他选项：B. science can help with the expression of emotions.：案例的论证方向是艺术帮助传播气候科学，而不是科学帮助艺术家表达情感，颠倒了作用方向。；C. public participation in science has a promising future.：听众接触气候信息不等于亲自参与科学研究，选项把“科学传播”扩大为“公众参与科研”。；D. art is effective in facilitating scientific innovations.：演出创新了科学传播方式，却没有推动新的科学发现或技术创新，混淆了传播与科研创新。
questions.evidence:
One example of how artists and scientists have together rocked the scenes came last month when the Sydney Symphony Orchestra performed a reworked version of Antonio Vivaldi's The Four Seasons.
They reimagined the 300-year-old score by injecting the latest climate prediction data for each season—provided by Monash University's Climate Change Communication Research Hub.
The performance was a creative call to action ahead of November's United Nations Climate Change Conference in Glasgow, UK.

questions.stem: Some artists seem to worry about ______ in the art-science partnership.
questions.explain:
正确项：their role may be underestimated. 有人强调艺术家不只是科学传播的助手，其作品也不应仅被当作研究对象；有价值的合作应让艺术家共同设计并评议项目。这说明艺术家担心自己的作用被局限在从属位置，未获充分重视。
其他选项：B. their reputation may be impaired.：文中担心的是合作地位和参与程度，不是个人声誉受损，属于概念偷换。；C. their creativity may be inhibited.：作者主张艺术家共同设计、相互评议，但没有说合作会压制其创造力；后文反而说合作能产生有感染力的艺术。；D. their work may be misguided.：文中说作品不应仅被当作研究对象，并未担心作品方向受到错误引导，属于无中生有。
questions.evidence:
Fewer artists than scientists responded to the Nature poll, however, several respondents noted that artists do not simply assist scientists with their communication requirements.
Nor should their work be considered only as an object of study.
The alliances are most valuable when scientists and artists have a shared stake in a project, are able to jointly design it and can critique each other's work.

questions.stem: What does the author say about CAYS?
options: It was headed alternately by artists and scientists.
Its projects aimed at advancing visual studies.
Its founders sought to raise the status of artists.
questions.explain:
正确项：It exemplified valuable art-science alliances. 题干沿用原卷所印的 CAYS；正文中的机构缩写为 CAVS。CAVS 以艺术家和科学家都感兴趣的“光”为合作基础，并期待研究人员与艺术家、作家、诗人的身份相互交融。这正是上一段所倡导的平等、双向且有共同关切的艺术科学联盟的实例。
其他选项：A. It was headed alternately by artists and scientists.：原文说两类人可以跨越身份开展合作，没有说中心负责人由艺术家和科学家轮流担任，属于无中生有。；C. Its projects aimed at advancing visual studies.：中心的目标是 explore the role of technology in culture；“视觉研究”得名于项目围绕光展开，并非项目旨在推进视觉研究学科，误把名称当成目的。；D. Its founders sought to raise the status of artists.：创办者追求的是跨学科合作和身份交融，并未提出提高艺术家社会地位，属于无中生有。
questions.evidence:
More than half a century ago, the Massachusetts Institute of Technology opened its Center for Advanced Visual Studies (CAVS) to explore the role of technology in culture.
Light was a something that both artists and scientists had an interest in, and therefore could form the basis of collaboration.
As science and technology progressed, and divided into more sub-disciplines, the centre was simultaneously looking to a time when leading researchers could also be artists, writers and poets, and vice versa.

questions.stem: In the last paragraph, the author holds that art-science collaborations
options: are likely to go beyond public expectations.
should do more than communicating science.
are becoming more popular than before.
questions.explain:
正确项：should do more than communicating science. 作者明确说艺术科学合作的作用范围要 go beyond 科研传播这一必要目的，即合作不能只承担向公众传播科学的功能，还应带来共同研究、创作、挑战与相互评议。
其他选项：A. are likely to go beyond public expectations.：原文要求合作超越的是 research communication 这一功能，不是超出公众预期，偷换了 go beyond 的宾语。；B. will intensify interdisciplinary competition.：末段强调双方投入、合作、接受挑战和评议，没有预测学科竞争加剧，混淆了 challenge 与竞争。；D. are becoming more popular than before.：as strong as ever 表示合作趋势依然强劲，并不等于“比过去更流行”；且末段重点在合作如何有效，而非流行度变化。
questions.evidence: The reach of art-science tie-ups needs to go beyond the necessary purpose of research communication, and participants must not fall into the trap of stereotyping each other.

reading.title: Text 4
reading.en_title: The personal grievance provisions of New Zealand's Employment Relation…
reading.cn_title: 新西兰解雇保护制度对劳动力市场的影响
reading.topic: 新西兰解雇保护制度对劳动力市场的影响
reading.intro: 本篇主题：新西兰解雇保护制度对劳动力市场的影响。先读题干，圈出关键词；回原文找证据句，再用主体、范围、方向排除。

paragraphs.en: The personal grievance provisions of New Zealand's Employment Relations Act 2000 (ERA) prevent an employer from firing an employee without good cause. Instead, dismissals must be justified. Employers must both show cause and act in a procedurally fair way.
paragraphs.zh: 新西兰《2000 年雇佣关系法》（ERA）中的个人申诉条款禁止雇主在没有正当理由的情况下解雇员工。 相反，任何解雇都必须有理有据。 雇主既要说明解雇理由，也必须依照公平程序行事。

paragraphs.en: Personal grievance procedures were designed to guard the jobs of ordinary workers from "unjustified dismissals". The premise was that the common law of contract lacked sufficient safeguards for workers against arbitrary conduct by management. Long gone are the days when a boss could simply give an employee contractual notice.
paragraphs.zh: 个人申诉程序旨在保护普通劳动者的工作，使其免遭“无正当理由的解雇”。 这一制度所依据的前提是，合同普通法不足以保护劳动者免受管理层任意行事的伤害。 老板只需按合同通知一声就能让员工走人的时代早已一去不复返。

paragraphs.en: But these provisions create difficulties for businesses when applied to highly paid managers and executives. As countless boards and business owners will attest, constraining firms from firing poorly performing, high-earning managers is a handbrake on boosting productivity and overall performance. The difference between C-grade and A-grade managers may very well be the difference between business success or failure. Between preserving the jobs of ordinary workers or losing them. Yet mediocrity is no longer enough to justify a dismissal.
paragraphs.zh: 但是，当这些条款适用于高薪经理和企业高管时，会给企业造成困难。 正如无数董事会和企业主都会证实的那样，限制企业解雇表现不佳的高薪经理，会拖累生产率和整体业绩的提升。 平庸经理与优秀经理之间的差距，很可能就是企业成功与失败之间的差距。 也可能就是保住普通劳动者的工作与让他们失业之间的差别。 然而，仅仅表现平庸已经不足以构成解雇理由。

paragraphs.en: Consequently—and paradoxically—laws introduced to protect the jobs of ordinary workers may be placing those jobs at risk.
paragraphs.zh: 因此，颇具悖论意味的是，为保护普通劳动者岗位而制定的法律，可能反而正在把这些岗位置于危险之中。

paragraphs.en: If not placing jobs at risk, to the extent employment protection laws constrain business owners from dismissing under-performing managers, those laws act as a constraint on firm productivity and therefore on workers' wages. Indeed, in "An International Perspective on New Zealand's Productivity Paradox" (2014), the Productivity Commission singled out the low quality of managerial capabilities as a cause of the country's poor productivity growth record.
paragraphs.zh: 即便这些法律尚未直接危及岗位，只要就业保护法限制企业主解雇绩效不佳的经理，它们就会制约企业生产率，进而压低劳动者工资。 事实上，生产率委员会在 2014 年的《新西兰生产率悖论的国际视角》中，特别指出管理能力低下是该国生产率增长不佳的一个原因。

paragraphs.en: Nor are highly paid managers themselves immune from the harm caused by the ERA's unjustified dismissal procedures. Because employment protection laws make it costlier to fire an employee, employers are more cautious about hiring new staff. This makes it harder for the marginal manager to gain employment. And firms pay staff less because firms carry the burden of the employment arrangement going wrong.
paragraphs.zh: 高薪经理自身也无法免受 ERA 不当解雇申诉程序所造成的伤害。 由于就业保护法提高了解雇员工的成本，雇主在招聘新员工时会更加谨慎。 这使得处于就业边缘的经理更难找到工作。 而且，由于企业必须承担雇佣安排出现问题的风险与成本，它们会给员工支付更低的薪酬。

paragraphs.en: Society also suffers from excessive employment protections. Stringent job dismissal regulations adversely affect productivity growth and hamper both prosperity and overall well-being.
paragraphs.zh: 社会同样会因过度的就业保护而受损。 严苛的解雇规定会对生产率增长产生不利影响，并阻碍经济繁荣和社会整体福祉的提升。

paragraphs.en: Across the Tasman Sea, Australia deals with the unjustified dismissal paradox by excluding employees earning above a specified "high-income threshold" from the protection of its unfair dismissal laws. In New Zealand, a 2016 private members' Bill tried to permit firms and high-income employees to contract out of the unjustified dismissal regime. However, the mechanisms proposed were unwieldy and the Bill was voted down following the change in government later that year.
paragraphs.zh: 在塔斯曼海另一边，澳大利亚的做法是把收入超过规定“高收入门槛”的员工排除在不公平解雇法的保护范围之外，以此应对不当解雇保护造成的悖论。 在新西兰，2016 年的一项议员私人法案曾试图允许企业与高收入员工通过合同约定，不适用不当解雇制度。 然而，法案提出的实施机制过于繁琐笨重；当年晚些时候政府更迭后，该法案在表决中被否决。

questions.stem: The personal grievance provisions of the ERA are intended to
options: protect the rights of ordinary workers.
questions.explain:
正确项：protect the rights of ordinary workers. 条款旨在保护普通劳动者的岗位，使其免遭无正当理由解雇，并弥补既有合同法无法充分防范管理层任意行为的问题。因此，其立法意图是保护普通劳动者的合法权益。
其他选项：A. punish dubious corporate practices.：制度是为员工提供免遭任意解雇的保障，而不是处罚所有可疑企业行为；选项扩大并改变了立法目的。；B. improve traditional hiring procedures.：条款规范的是解雇理由和程序，不是传统招聘流程，混淆了雇佣关系的进入与退出。；C. exempt employers from certain duties.：法律要求雇主说明理由并遵守公平程序，是增加其义务而非免除义务，与原文相反。
questions.evidence:
Personal grievance procedures were designed to guard the jobs of ordinary workers from "unjustified dismissals".
The premise was that the common law of contract lacked sufficient safeguards for workers against arbitrary conduct by management.

questions.stem: It can be learned from Paragraph 3 that the provisions may
options: affect the public image of the firms.
questions.explain:
正确项：hinder business development. 条款使企业难以解雇低绩效高薪经理，成为提升生产率和整体业绩的阻力；管理者质量甚至可能决定企业成败。因此，这些规定可能妨碍企业发展。
其他选项：B. undermine managers' authority.：受条款保护、难以被解雇的正是经理；文中讨论的是经理能力影响企业绩效，并未说其管理权威受到削弱。；C. affect the public image of the firms.：段落只谈生产率、经营表现和成败，没有涉及企业公众形象，属于无中生有。；D. worsen labor-management relations.：文中没有描述劳资双方关系恶化，核心问题是低绩效管理者难以被替换，偷换了影响对象。
questions.evidence:
As countless boards and business owners will attest, constraining firms from firing poorly performing, high-earning managers is a handbrake on boosting productivity and overall performance.
The difference between C-grade and A-grade managers may very well be the difference between business success or failure.

questions.stem: Which of the following measures would the Productivity Commission support?
options: Limiting the powers of business owners.
questions.explain:
正确项：Dismissing poorly performing managers. 生产率委员会把管理能力低下特别列为新西兰生产率增长不佳的原因；上文又指出保护法限制企业解雇低绩效经理会制约生产率。由此可知，委员会的判断逻辑支持淘汰表现不佳的经理。
其他选项：A. Imposing reasonable wage restraints.：工资受压低是生产率受限的后果，文中没有主张人为限制工资，倒置了因果链条。；B. Enforcing employment protection laws.：作者所述就业保护法正是企业难以解雇低绩效经理的原因；强化这类法律不能解决委员会指出的管理质量问题。；C. Limiting the powers of business owners.：原文认为企业主解雇低绩效管理者受到过多限制，合理推论是放宽而非进一步限制其权力。
questions.evidence:
If not placing jobs at risk, to the extent employment protection laws constrain business owners from dismissing under-performing managers, those laws act as a constraint on firm productivity and therefore on workers' wages.
Indeed, in "An International Perspective on New Zealand's Productivity Paradox" (2014), the Productivity Commission singled out the low quality of managerial capabilities as a cause of the country's poor productivity growth record.

questions.stem: What might be an effect of ERA's unjustified dismissal procedures?
options: Highly paid managers lose their jobs.
Society sees a rise in overall well-being.
Employers need to hire new staff.
questions.explain:
正确项：Employees suffer from salary cuts. 不当解雇程序提高了解雇成本，使企业承担雇佣关系失败的风险；企业因而会给员工支付更低薪酬。pay staff less 直接对应员工遭遇工资削减或薪酬水平下降。
其他选项：A. Highly paid managers lose their jobs.：保护程序使解雇更加昂贵和困难，高薪经理受到的伤害主要是边缘求职者更难获聘，而不是在职者更容易失业，与机制相反。；C. Society sees a rise in overall well-being.：下一段明确说严格的解雇规定会妨碍繁荣和整体福祉，选项把不利影响说成上升，与原文相反。；D. Employers need to hire new staff.：原文说雇主会对招聘新员工更加谨慎，没有说他们产生了招聘需求，偷换了“招聘态度”与“招聘需要”。
questions.evidence:
Because employment protection laws make it costlier to fire an employee, employers are more cautious about hiring new staff.
And firms pay staff less because firms carry the burden of the employment arrangement going wrong.

questions.stem: It can be inferred that the "high-income threshold" in Australia
options: is difficult to put into practice.
questions.explain:
正确项：is beneficial to business owners. 收入超过门槛的员工不受不公平解雇法保护，这使企业主能够更灵活地解雇表现不佳的高薪管理者，避免过度保护对生产率和经营表现的拖累。因此，该门槛有利于企业主。
其他选项：A. has secured managers' earnings.：高收入门槛是取消高薪员工的解雇保护，并非保障其收入；相反，他们的职位保障会减少。；B. has produced undesired results.：作者把澳大利亚做法作为应对制度悖论的方案，没有提到它造成不良后果，属于无中生有。；D. is difficult to put into practice.：unwieldy 描述的是新西兰 2016 年法案所提机制，不能张冠李戴到澳大利亚已经实施的高收入门槛上。
questions.evidence: Across the Tasman Sea, Australia deals with the unjustified dismissal paradox by excluding employees earning above a specified "high-income threshold" from the protection of its unfair dismissal laws.

sentences.en: All of which creates huge headaches for institutions, such as museums, trying to preserve culturally important objects.
sentences.core: All of which creates huge headaches for institutions.
sentences.structure: All of which 概括前文塑料开裂、渗出添加剂和化为浆状物等现象；such as museums 举例说明 institutions；trying to preserve... 是现在分词短语，修饰这些机构。
sentences.key: headache：常见义为“头痛”；此处比喻“棘手的问题、麻烦事”。
sentences.zh: 所有这些变化都给博物馆等试图保存具有文化价值物品的机构带来了巨大的难题。
sentences.tip: which 指前述全部劣化现象，不是只指最近一句的 sludge。

sentences.en: Certain artifacts are especially vulnerable because some pioneers in plastic art didn't always know how to mix ingredients properly, says Thea van Oosten, a polymer chemist who, until retiring a few years ago, worked for decades at the Cultural Heritage Agency of the Netherlands (RCE).
sentences.core: Certain artifacts are especially vulnerable, says Thea van Oosten.
sentences.structure: because... 说明这些艺术品脆弱的原因；a polymer chemist 是人物同位语；who...worked for decades... 是修饰该化学家的定语从句，其中 until retiring... 是插入的时间状语。
sentences.key: vulnerable：常见义为“易受伤的”；此处指材料“容易受损、容易劣化”。；ingredient：常用于指“烹饪原料”；此处指制作塑料艺术品所用的“配料、组分”。
sentences.zh: 聚合物化学家西娅·范·奥斯滕说，某些艺术品格外脆弱，是因为一些塑料艺术的先驱当年并不总是知道怎样正确调配原料；她在几年前退休之前，曾在荷兰文化遗产局（RCE）工作数十年。
sentences.tip: 先找谓语，再拆从句；把修饰语挂回它修饰的词。

sentences.en: Those pieces included small beds of roses and other items as well as a few dozen "nature carpets"—large rectangles decorated with foam pumpkins, cabbages, and watermelons.
sentences.core: Those pieces included A as well as B.
sentences.structure: as well as 连接两类作品；破折号后的 large rectangles... 是对 nature carpets 的同位解释；decorated with... 是过去分词短语，说明地毯上的装饰。
sentences.key: bed：常见义为“床”；a bed of roses 在此指种有玫瑰的“花坛、花圃”，不是习语“安逸的处境”。
sentences.zh: 这些作品包括小片玫瑰花圃等物件，也包括几十张“自然地毯”——装饰着泡沫塑料南瓜、卷心菜和西瓜的大幅长方形作品。
sentences.tip: 先找谓语，再拆从句；把修饰语挂回它修饰的词。

sentences.en: He wanted viewers to walk around on the carpets—which meant they had to be durable.
sentences.core: He wanted viewers to walk around on the carpets.
sentences.structure: 破折号后的 which 指代前面“让参观者在地毯上走动”这件事；they 指 the carpets。
sentences.key: 见下方词汇笔记
sentences.zh: 他希望参观者能在这些地毯上走动——这意味着它们必须经久耐用。
sentences.tip: 先找谓语，再拆从句；把修饰语挂回它修饰的词。

sentences.en: Museums locked some of them away in the dark.
sentences.core: Museums locked some of them away.
sentences.structure: them 指上一句中正在开裂、碎裂的吉拉尔迪作品；in the dark 说明保存环境。
sentences.key: lock sth. away：把某物锁藏起来，使其不再被使用或展示。
sentences.zh: 博物馆把其中一些作品锁进了不见光的地方。
sentences.tip: 先找谓语，再拆从句；把修饰语挂回它修饰的词。

sentences.en: She is proud that several sculptures have even gone on display again, albeit sometimes beneath protective cases.
sentences.core: She is proud that several sculptures have gone on display again.
sentences.structure: that... 是说明自豪内容的从句；albeit... 补充让步信息，指出重新展出仍附带保护条件。
sentences.key: go on display：被展出、公开陈列。；albeit：尽管、虽然，相当于 although，但其后常直接接短语而非完整从句。
sentences.zh: 令她自豪的是，有几件雕塑甚至已经重新展出，尽管有时需要放在保护罩下。
sentences.tip: 先找谓语，再拆从句；把修饰语挂回它修饰的词。

sentences.en: Despite success stories like van Oosten's, preservation of plastics will likely get harder.
sentences.core: Preservation of plastics will likely get harder.
sentences.structure: Despite... 引出让步背景；van Oosten's 省略了 success story。
sentences.key: story：常见义为“故事”；success story 指“成功案例”。
sentences.zh: 尽管有范·奥斯滕这样的成功案例，塑料制品的保存工作很可能仍会变得更加艰难。
sentences.tip: 先找谓语，再拆从句；把修饰语挂回它修饰的词。

sentences.en: Worse, biodegradable plastics, designed to disintegrate, are increasingly common.
sentences.core: Biodegradable plastics are increasingly common.
sentences.structure: designed to disintegrate 是过去分词短语，补充说明这类塑料的设计目的。
sentences.key: biodegradable：可生物降解的。；disintegrate：瓦解、分解成碎片。
sentences.zh: 更糟的是，本来就被设计成会分解的可生物降解塑料正变得越来越常见。
sentences.tip: 先找谓语，再拆从句；把修饰语挂回它修饰的词。

sentences.en: Joana Lia Ferreira, an assistant professor of conservation and restoration at the NOVA School of Science and Technology, notes that archaeologists first defined the great material ages of human history—Stone Age, Iron Age, and so on—after examining artifacts in museums.
sentences.core: Joana Lia Ferreira notes that archaeologists defined the great material ages.
sentences.structure: 人名后的长同位语交代其职务；that... 是 notes 的宾语从句；两个短横线之间列举 material ages；after examining... 说明时代划分所依据的材料。
sentences.key: age：常见义为“年龄”；此处指具有特定历史文化特征的“时代”。
sentences.zh: 诺瓦科技学院文物保护与修复专业助理教授若阿娜·莉娅·费雷拉指出，考古学家正是在研究了博物馆藏品之后，才首次划分出人类历史上以材料命名的各大时代，例如石器时代、铁器时代等。
sentences.tip: 先找谓语，再拆从句；把修饰语挂回它修饰的词。

sentences.en: We now live in an age of plastic, she says, "and what we decide to collect today, what we decide to preserve...will have a strong impact on how in the future we'll be seen."
sentences.core: What we decide to collect today and what we decide to preserve will have a strong impact.
sentences.structure: 两个并列的 what 从句共同作主语；on how...we'll be seen 说明影响的对象，其中是被动语态。
sentences.key: see：常见义为“看见”；此处是“看待、认识、评价”。；break down easily：容易分解、降解。；create huge headaches for：给……造成巨大的难题。；be vulnerable to light damage：容易受到光照损害。
sentences.zh: 她说，我们如今生活在一个塑料时代，“而我们今天决定收藏什么、保存什么……将深刻影响未来的人如何看待我们”。
sentences.tip: we 指当代人；隐含的观察者是未来的人。句子强调今日保存塑料藏品对后世理解当代社会的历史意义，而非对今日文化生活的影响。

sentences.en: As the latest crop of students pen their undergraduate application form and weigh up their options, it may be worth considering just how the point, purpose and value of a degree has changed and what Generation Z need to consider as they start the third stage of their educational journey.
sentences.core: It may be worth considering A and B.
sentences.structure: As... 是时间状语从句；how...has changed 与 what...need to consider 是两个并列的宾语从句；第二个从句中的 as... 表示“当他们开始……时”。
sentences.key: crop：常见义为“庄稼、收成”；此处指同一时期出现的“一批”学生。；pen：常见义为“钢笔”；此处作动词，意为“书写、填写”。；point：常见义为“点、分数”；此处指做某事的“意义、用处”。；weigh up one's options：权衡某人可以作出的各种选择。
sentences.zh: 当最新一批学生填写本科申请表、权衡各种选择时，或许值得认真思考：大学学位的意义、目的与价值究竟发生了怎样的变化，以及 Z 世代在开启教育历程的第三阶段时需要考虑什么。
sentences.tip: it 是形式主语，真正值得考虑的是后面两个疑问从句；作者要求重新审视的是学位本身的意义和必要性，而不只是如何选学校。

sentences.en: Millennials were told that if you did well in school, got a decent degree, you would be set up for life.
sentences.core: Millennials were told that...
sentences.structure: that 引导所告知的内容；其中 if you did well...and got... 是条件从句，you would be set up for life 是结果。
sentences.key: decent：常见义为“体面的”；此处指质量或水平“相当不错的、过得去的”。；be set up for life：不是“为生活作好一般准备”，而是指经济或事业基础已经稳固，因而“一生有保障”。
sentences.zh: 千禧一代曾被告知，只要在学校表现良好、取得一个不错的学位，一辈子的生活就有了保障。
sentences.tip: 先找谓语，再拆从句；把修饰语挂回它修饰的词。

sentences.en: Today, 28 per cent of graduates in the UK are in non-graduate roles, a percentage which is double the average among the OECD countries.
sentences.core: 28 per cent of graduates in the UK are in non-graduate roles.
sentences.structure: 逗号后的 a percentage 是对 28 per cent 的同位说明；which... 是定语从句，补充该比例与 OECD 平均水平的比较。
sentences.key: non-graduate role：不是“非毕业生的身份”，而是“不要求大学学历的岗位”。
sentences.zh: 如今，英国有 28% 的大学毕业生从事并不要求大学学历的工作，这一比例是经济合作与发展组织成员国平均水平的两倍。
sentences.tip: 先找谓语，再拆从句；把修饰语挂回它修饰的词。

sentences.en: This is not to say that there is no point in getting a degree, but rather stress that a degree is not for everyone, that the switch from classroom to lecture hall is not an inevitable one and that other options are available.
sentences.core: This is not to say A, but rather (to) stress B.
sentences.structure: not...but rather... 先排除极端理解，再说明真正观点；stress 后接三个并列的 that 从句：学位并非适合所有人、升大学并非必然、另有其他选择。
sentences.key: point：there is no point in doing sth. 表示“做某事没有意义”。；switch：此处作名词，指从中学到大学的“转变、转换”。；lecture hall：大学讲堂；这里借指大学教育。
sentences.zh: 这并不是说取得学位毫无意义，而是要强调：学位并不适合每一个人；从中学课堂转入大学讲堂并非必然选择；此外还有其他道路可走。
sentences.tip: 作者不是否定大学教育的全部价值，而是反对把上大学视为人人必须遵循的默认路径。

sentences.en: Thankfully, there are signs that this is already happening, with Generation Z seeking to learn from their millennial predecessors, even if parents and teachers tend to be still set in the degree mindset.
sentences.core: There are signs that this is already happening.
sentences.structure: that... 是解释 signs 内容的同位语从句；with Generation Z seeking... 补充伴随情况；even if... 引出让步背景。
sentences.key: predecessor：前任、前辈；此处指年龄较长、先经历大学教育与就业的千禧一代。；be set in：固定于、固守于某种想法或做法。
sentences.zh: 令人欣慰的是，已经有迹象表明这种转变正在发生：Z 世代正努力从千禧一代前辈的经历中吸取教训，尽管父母和教师往往仍受“唯学位”思维束缚。
sentences.tip: this 回指上一段所说“不把大学视为必然选择、考虑其他道路”的转变。

sentences.en: Many too are seeing the advantages of scrapping a degree requirement for certain roles.
sentences.core: Many are seeing the advantages.
sentences.structure: Many 承接上一句，指许多雇主；of scrapping... 说明他们认识到的是何种好处。
sentences.key: scrap：常见义为“碎片、废料”；此处作动词，意为“取消、废除”。
sentences.zh: 许多雇主也开始认识到，取消某些岗位的学历要求是有好处的。
sentences.tip: 先找谓语，再拆从句；把修饰语挂回它修饰的词。

sentences.en: For those for whom a degree is the desired route, consider that this may well be the first of many.
sentences.core: Consider that this may be the first of many.
sentences.structure: For those... 指建议适用的人群；for whom a degree is the desired route 是定语从句，修饰 those；this 指即将攻读的第一个学位；many 后省略 degrees。
sentences.key: 见下方词汇笔记
sentences.zh: 对于那些确实希望走学位教育这条路的人，应当想到：这个学位很可能只是以后多个学位中的第一个。
sentences.tip: 先找谓语，再拆从句；把修饰语挂回它修饰的词。

sentences.en: It is unlikely that Generation Z will be done with education at 18 or 21; they will need to be constantly upskilling throughout their career to stay employable.
sentences.core: It is unlikely that Generation Z will be done with education; they will need to be upskilling.
sentences.structure: It 是形式主语，that... 是真正主语；分号连接“教育不会早早结束”与“职业生涯持续学习”两个紧密相关的判断；to stay employable 表目的。
sentences.key: be done with：结束、不再继续做某事。；upskill：提升技能、学习更高级或更新的职业技能。；employable：具备受雇条件的、有就业竞争力的。
sentences.zh: Z 世代不太可能在 18 岁或 21 岁时就结束教育；为了始终具备就业竞争力，他们需要在整个职业生涯中不断提升技能。
sentences.tip: 先找谓语，再拆从句；把修饰语挂回它修饰的词。

sentences.en: It has been estimated that this generation, due to the pressures of technology, the wish for personal fulfilment and desire for diversity, will work for 17 different employers over the course of their working life and have five different careers.
sentences.core: It has been estimated that this generation will work for 17 different employers and have five different careers.
sentences.structure: It 是形式主语；that... 是真正主语；三个并列名词短语置于主语之后作原因状语；work for... 与 have... 是并列谓语。
sentences.key: personal fulfilment：个人价值的实现、个人成就感。；over the course of：在……的整个过程中。
sentences.zh: 据估计，由于技术发展带来的压力、实现个人价值的愿望以及追求多样性的需求，这一代人在整个职业生涯中将为 17 个不同的雇主工作，并经历 5 种不同的职业。
sentences.tip: 先找谓语，再拆从句；把修饰语挂回它修饰的词。

sentences.en: Education, and not just knowledge gained on campus, will be a core part of Generation Z's career trajectory.
sentences.core: Education will be a core part of Generation Z's career trajectory.
sentences.structure: and not just knowledge gained on campus 是插入成分，强调教育不限于大学校园内一次性获得的知识。
sentences.key: trajectory：本义为物体运动的“轨迹”；此处指职业生涯的“发展路径、走向”。
sentences.zh: 教育，而且不只是校园里获得的知识，将成为 Z 世代职业发展轨迹的核心组成部分。
sentences.tip: 先找谓语，再拆从句；把修饰语挂回它修饰的词。

sentences.en: Their sons or daughters would never say such a thing; it's as if they already know that their degree won't define them in the same way.
sentences.core: Their sons or daughters would never say such a thing; it's as if they know...
sentences.structure: as if 引导方式从句；其中 that... 作 know 的宾语。
sentences.key: define：常见义为“下定义”；此处指“界定一个人的身份和人生”。；weigh up one's options：权衡各种选择。；be set up for life：一生有保障。；be found wanting：被证明有缺陷、未达到预期。
sentences.zh: 他们的子女绝不会这样说；仿佛年轻一代已经明白，学位不会再以同样的方式定义自己的身份。
sentences.tip: 先找谓语，再拆从句；把修饰语挂回它修饰的词。

sentences.en: These were some of the words that Nature readers used to describe their experience of art-science collaborations in a series of articles on partnerships between artists and researchers.
sentences.core: These were some of the words.
sentences.structure: that Nature readers used... 是定语从句，修饰 words；on partnerships... 修饰 a series of articles，说明系列文章的主题。
sentences.key: 见下方词汇笔记
sentences.zh: 在一组探讨艺术家与研究人员合作关系的文章中，《自然》杂志的读者用上述词语来形容他们参与艺术与科学合作的体验。
sentences.tip: their experience 指读者亲身参与跨界合作的体验，不是阅读这些文章的体验。

sentences.en: Nearly 40% of the roughly 350 people who responded to an accompanying poll said they had collaborated with artists; and almost all said they would consider doing so in future.
sentences.core: Nearly 40% said A; and almost all said B.
sentences.structure: who responded... 是定语从句，修饰 people；两个 said 后分别接省略了 that 的宾语从句。
sentences.key: accompanying：此处指与系列文章一同发布、作为配套内容的。；do so：代替前面的 collaborate with artists，意为“与艺术家合作”。
sentences.zh: 在参加配套调查的大约 350 人中，近 40% 表示自己曾与艺术家合作；而且几乎所有人都表示，将来会考虑开展这类合作。
sentences.tip: 先找谓语，再拆从句；把修饰语挂回它修饰的词。

sentences.en: "Artists help scientists reach a broader audience and make emotional connections that enhance learning," one respondent said.
sentences.core: Artists help scientists reach...and make...connections.
sentences.structure: help + 宾语 + 动词原形；reach 与 make 是并列补语；that enhance learning 是修饰 emotional connections 的定语从句。
sentences.key: 见下方词汇笔记
sentences.zh: 一名调查参与者说：“艺术家帮助科学家触及更广泛的受众，并建立能够促进理解与学习的情感联系。”
sentences.tip: 先找谓语，再拆从句；把修饰语挂回它修饰的词。

sentences.en: One example of how artists and scientists have together rocked the scenes came last month when the Sydney Symphony Orchestra performed a reworked version of Antonio Vivaldi's The Four Seasons.
sentences.core: One example came last month.
sentences.structure: of how... 说明这是哪一方面的例子；when... 是时间状语从句，交代具体事件。
sentences.key: rock the scene：此处不是字面上的“摇动场景”，而是指“震撼现场、带来轰动”。；reworked：重新加工或改编的。
sentences.zh: 艺术家与科学家携手带来轰动效果的一个例子出现在上个月：悉尼交响乐团演奏了安东尼奥·维瓦尔第《四季》的改编版。
sentences.tip: 先找谓语，再拆从句；把修饰语挂回它修饰的词。

sentences.en: They reimagined the 300-year-old score by injecting the latest climate prediction data for each season—provided by Monash University's Climate Change Communication Research Hub.
sentences.core: They reimagined the score.
sentences.structure: by injecting... 说明改编方式；provided by... 是过去分词短语，修饰 climate prediction data，不是修饰 each season。
sentences.key: score：常见义为“分数”；此处作名词，指音乐作品的“总谱、乐谱”。；inject：常见义为“注射”；此处指把气候数据“注入、融入”艺术作品。；reimagine：以新的方式重新构想、重新诠释。
sentences.zh: 他们把莫纳什大学气候变化传播研究中心提供的各季最新气候预测数据融入这部有 300 年历史的乐谱，从而对其作出全新诠释。
sentences.tip: 先找谓语，再拆从句；把修饰语挂回它修饰的词。

sentences.en: Fewer artists than scientists responded to the Nature poll, however, several respondents noted that artists do not simply assist scientists with their communication requirements.
sentences.core: Fewer artists responded; several respondents noted that...
sentences.structure: fewer...than... 比较艺术家与科学家的参与人数；however 标记转折；that... 是 noted 的宾语从句。
sentences.key: requirement：此处指科学家在传播科研内容方面的“需要、需求”。
sentences.zh: 不过，参与《自然》杂志调查的艺术家少于科学家；几名调查参与者指出，艺术家并不只是帮助科学家满足科研传播需求的助手。
sentences.tip: 先找谓语，再拆从句；把修饰语挂回它修饰的词。

sentences.en: Nor should their work be considered only as an object of study.
sentences.core: Their work should not be considered only as an object of study.
sentences.structure: 否定副词 Nor 置于句首引起部分倒装，助动词 should 提到主语之前；their 指艺术家。
sentences.key: 见下方词汇笔记
sentences.zh: 艺术家的作品也不应仅仅被视为研究对象。
sentences.tip: 本句进一步反对把艺术及艺术家降为科学研究的工具或对象，核心是艺术方的地位不能被低估。

sentences.en: The alliances are most valuable when scientists and artists have a shared stake in a project, are able to jointly design it and can critique each other's work.
sentences.core: The alliances are most valuable when scientists and artists do A, B and C.
sentences.structure: when 从句中，have、are able to design、can critique 是三个并列谓语；it 指 a project。
sentences.key: stake：常见义为“木桩、股份”；have a shared stake in 指“共同利益攸关、共同承担项目成败”。；critique：对作品作出深入、专业的评议，并不只是一般的“批评”。
sentences.zh: 当科学家和艺术家共同关心项目的成败，能够一起设计项目并相互评议对方的工作时，这种合作关系才最有价值。
sentences.tip: 先找谓语，再拆从句；把修饰语挂回它修饰的词。

sentences.en: Light was a something that both artists and scientists had an interest in, and therefore could form the basis of collaboration.
sentences.core: Light was something and therefore could form the basis of collaboration.
sentences.structure: that both artists and scientists had an interest in 是定语从句，修饰 something；therefore 引出共同兴趣带来的结果。
sentences.key: 见下方词汇笔记
sentences.zh: 光是艺术家与科学家都感兴趣的事物，因此能够成为双方合作的基础。
sentences.tip: 原卷印作 a something，语义上仍应把 something 理解为“某种双方都感兴趣的事物”。

sentences.en: As science and technology progressed, and divided into more sub-disciplines, the centre was simultaneously looking to a time when leading researchers could also be artists, writers and poets, and vice versa.
sentences.core: The centre was looking to a time.
sentences.structure: As... 是时间与趋势状语从句；when... 是定语从句，修饰 a time；and vice versa 将前述身份关系反向成立。
sentences.key: look to：此处指“展望、期待”未来，而不是简单地“看向”。；vice versa：反之亦然，即艺术家、作家和诗人也可以成为研究人员。
sentences.zh: 随着科学技术不断发展并细分出更多学科，这一中心同时也在展望一个时代：顶尖研究人员也可以成为艺术家、作家和诗人，反之亦然。
sentences.tip: 先找谓语，再拆从句；把修饰语挂回它修饰的词。

sentences.en: Nature's poll findings suggest that this trend is as strong as ever, but, to make a collaboration work, both sides need to invest time, and embrace surprise and challenge.
sentences.core: The findings suggest A, but both sides need B.
sentences.structure: that... 是 suggest 的宾语从句；to make... 是目的状语；invest 与 embrace 是并列谓语。
sentences.key: as strong as ever：一如既往地强劲。；make sth. work：使某事顺利运转、取得成效。；embrace surprise and challenge：主动接受意外情况和挑战。
sentences.zh: 《自然》杂志的调查结果表明，这一合作趋势依旧十分强劲；但是，要让合作真正奏效，双方都需要投入时间，并欣然接受意外与挑战。
sentences.tip: 先找谓语，再拆从句；把修饰语挂回它修饰的词。

sentences.en: The reach of art-science tie-ups needs to go beyond the necessary purpose of research communication, and participants must not fall into the trap of stereotyping each other.
sentences.core: The reach needs to go beyond...and participants must not fall into...
sentences.structure: go beyond 与 must not fall into 由 and 连接，提出两项合作原则。
sentences.key: reach：常见义为“到达”；此处作名词，指合作所能发挥作用的“范围、影响范围”。；tie-up：合作关系、联合行动。；stereotype：把某人简单地套入刻板印象。
sentences.zh: 艺术与科学合作的作用范围需要超越科研传播这一必要目的，参与者也绝不能落入彼此刻板化的陷阱。
sentences.tip: 作者并未否认科研传播的必要性，而是说合作不能止步于此，还应共同研究、创作与相互评议。

sentences.en: The premise was that the common law of contract lacked sufficient safeguards for workers against arbitrary conduct by management.
sentences.core: The premise was that the common law lacked safeguards.
sentences.structure: that... 是表语从句，解释制度设计的前提；for workers 指保障对象；against arbitrary conduct... 指所防范的风险。
sentences.key: premise：前提、作为制度或论证出发点的假设。；safeguard：保障措施、保护机制。；arbitrary：任意的、缺乏合理依据或约束的。
sentences.zh: 这一制度所依据的前提是，合同普通法不足以保护劳动者免受管理层任意行事的伤害。
sentences.tip: 先找谓语，再拆从句；把修饰语挂回它修饰的词。

sentences.en: Long gone are the days when a boss could simply give an employee contractual notice.
sentences.core: The days are long gone.
sentences.structure: 表语 Long gone 置于句首引起完全倒装；when... 是定语从句，修饰 the days。
sentences.key: contractual notice：合同约定的解雇通知，即依合同提前通知员工终止雇佣关系。
sentences.zh: 老板只需按合同通知一声就能让员工走人的时代早已一去不复返。
sentences.tip: 先找谓语，再拆从句；把修饰语挂回它修饰的词。

sentences.en: But these provisions create difficulties for businesses when applied to highly paid managers and executives.
sentences.core: These provisions create difficulties for businesses.
sentences.structure: when applied... 是省略了 they are 的时间或条件状语从句，they 指这些条款。
sentences.key: 见下方词汇笔记
sentences.zh: 但是，当这些条款适用于高薪经理和企业高管时，会给企业造成困难。
sentences.tip: 先找谓语，再拆从句；把修饰语挂回它修饰的词。

sentences.en: As countless boards and business owners will attest, constraining firms from firing poorly performing, high-earning managers is a handbrake on boosting productivity and overall performance.
sentences.core: Constraining firms ... is a handbrake on boosting productivity and performance.
sentences.structure: As...will attest 是方式状语从句；动名词短语 constraining firms... 作主语；from firing... 说明限制企业做什么。
sentences.key: attest：证实、证明某事属实。；handbrake：本义为“手刹”；此处比喻妨碍发展或进步的“阻力、拖累”。
sentences.zh: 正如无数董事会和企业主都会证实的那样，限制企业解雇表现不佳的高薪经理，会拖累生产率和整体业绩的提升。
sentences.tip: 先找谓语，再拆从句；把修饰语挂回它修饰的词。

sentences.en: Between preserving the jobs of ordinary workers or losing them.
sentences.core: 本句是承接上一句的省略结构，完整意思为 The difference may be the difference between preserving...and losing...。
sentences.structure: 见原句
sentences.key: 见下方词汇笔记
sentences.zh: 也可能就是保住普通劳动者的工作与让他们失业之间的差别。
sentences.tip: them 指 the jobs of ordinary workers，也可从结果上理解为普通劳动者失去工作；其因果链是管理低效导致企业失败，最终危及普通岗位。

sentences.en: Consequently—and paradoxically—laws introduced to protect the jobs of ordinary workers may be placing those jobs at risk.
sentences.core: Laws may be placing those jobs at risk.
sentences.structure: introduced to protect... 是过去分词短语，修饰 laws；those jobs 回指 the jobs of ordinary workers。
sentences.key: paradoxically：自相矛盾地、看似矛盾却可能真实地。；place sth. at risk：使某事物面临风险。
sentences.zh: 因此，颇具悖论意味的是，为保护普通劳动者岗位而制定的法律，可能反而正在把这些岗位置于危险之中。
sentences.tip: 先找谓语，再拆从句；把修饰语挂回它修饰的词。

sentences.en: If not placing jobs at risk, to the extent employment protection laws constrain business owners from dismissing under-performing managers, those laws act as a constraint on firm productivity and therefore on workers' wages.
sentences.core: Those laws act as a constraint on firm productivity and workers' wages.
sentences.structure: If not placing jobs at risk 表示退一步假设“即便没有危及岗位”；to the extent... 说明限制产生的条件与程度；therefore 串联生产率与工资的因果关系。
sentences.key: to the extent：在……的程度上；结合语境可译为“只要、就……而言”。；act as a constraint on：构成对……的制约。
sentences.zh: 即便这些法律尚未直接危及岗位，只要就业保护法限制企业主解雇绩效不佳的经理，它们就会制约企业生产率，进而压低劳动者工资。
sentences.tip: and therefore on workers' wages 承接的是 a constraint on，即法律也间接制约工资，而不是保护工资。

sentences.en: Indeed, in "An International Perspective on New Zealand's Productivity Paradox" (2014), the Productivity Commission singled out the low quality of managerial capabilities as a cause of the country's poor productivity growth record.
sentences.core: The Productivity Commission singled out the low quality ... as a cause.
sentences.structure: 书名和年份所在介词短语交代出处；of the country's poor productivity growth record 修饰 a cause。
sentences.key: single out A as B：特别指出或选出 A，认定其为 B。；record：常见义为“记录”；此处指一段时期内表现出来的“业绩、表现”。
sentences.zh: 事实上，生产率委员会在 2014 年的《新西兰生产率悖论的国际视角》中，特别指出管理能力低下是该国生产率增长不佳的一个原因。
sentences.tip: 先找谓语，再拆从句；把修饰语挂回它修饰的词。

sentences.en: Nor are highly paid managers themselves immune from the harm caused by the ERA's unjustified dismissal procedures.
sentences.core: Highly paid managers are not immune from the harm.
sentences.structure: 否定词 Nor 置于句首引起部分倒装；caused by... 是过去分词短语，修饰 harm。
sentences.key: be immune from：不受……影响、免受……伤害。
sentences.zh: 高薪经理自身也无法免受 ERA 不当解雇申诉程序所造成的伤害。
sentences.tip: 先找谓语，再拆从句；把修饰语挂回它修饰的词。

sentences.en: Because employment protection laws make it costlier to fire an employee, employers are more cautious about hiring new staff.
sentences.core: Employers are more cautious about hiring new staff.
sentences.structure: Because... 说明招聘趋于谨慎的原因；make it costlier to fire... 中 it 是形式宾语，to fire... 是真正宾语。
sentences.key: 见下方词汇笔记
sentences.zh: 由于就业保护法提高了解雇员工的成本，雇主在招聘新员工时会更加谨慎。
sentences.tip: 先找谓语，再拆从句；把修饰语挂回它修饰的词。

sentences.en: And firms pay staff less because firms carry the burden of the employment arrangement going wrong.
sentences.core: Firms pay staff less because firms carry the burden.
sentences.structure: of the employment arrangement going wrong 中，the employment arrangement 是动名词 going wrong 的逻辑主语。
sentences.key: carry the burden of：承担……的负担、风险或成本。；go wrong：出问题、未按预期发展。
sentences.zh: 而且，由于企业必须承担雇佣安排出现问题的风险与成本，它们会给员工支付更低的薪酬。
sentences.tip: 先找谓语，再拆从句；把修饰语挂回它修饰的词。

sentences.en: Across the Tasman Sea, Australia deals with the unjustified dismissal paradox by excluding employees earning above a specified "high-income threshold" from the protection of its unfair dismissal laws.
sentences.core: Australia deals with the paradox by excluding employees from the protection.
sentences.structure: earning above... 是现在分词短语，修饰 employees；by excluding... 说明解决方式。
sentences.key: across the Tasman Sea：塔斯曼海位于澳大利亚与新西兰之间，此处用来引出澳大利亚的对比做法。；threshold：门槛、触发某项规则的临界值。；exclude A from B：将 A 排除在 B 之外。
sentences.zh: 在塔斯曼海另一边，澳大利亚的做法是把收入超过规定“高收入门槛”的员工排除在不公平解雇法的保护范围之外，以此应对不当解雇保护造成的悖论。
sentences.tip: 先找谓语，再拆从句；把修饰语挂回它修饰的词。

sentences.en: However, the mechanisms proposed were unwieldy and the Bill was voted down following the change in government later that year.
sentences.core: The mechanisms were unwieldy and the Bill was voted down.
sentences.structure: proposed 是过去分词，修饰 mechanisms；following... 表示“在……之后”。
sentences.key: unwieldy：笨重难用的；此处指机制复杂、难以操作。；vote down：投票否决。；without good cause：没有正当理由。；act in a procedurally fair way：依照公平程序行事。
sentences.zh: 然而，法案提出的实施机制过于繁琐笨重；当年晚些时候政府更迭后，该法案在表决中被否决。
sentences.tip: 难以实施并被否决的是新西兰 2016 年法案，不是澳大利亚已经采用的“高收入门槛”；不能据此选择“澳大利亚门槛难以实施”。
